title: Asked by parda: Adopt the hot-path forest prototyped in parda-2d (Forest, Flat, Column) as a sylva module
body:
Adopt the hot-path forest prototyped in parda-2d (Forest, Flat, Column) as a sylva module (graft:01a10a64-df76..452c, from parda)

What was needed:
- parda: Move parda-2d's crates/sylva-forest (github.com/vaibhav-gopal/parda2D at 7912896; written against sylva 9d2a15d) into sylva as a module beside tree and graph, then publish. What it is: (1) Forest: ids are (slot index, generation), removing bumps the generation so stale ids fail safely, freed slots are reused; intrusive links per node (parent, first/last child, prev/next sibling, one 20-byte record per node) for O(1) push, insert-before, move and detach and O(subtree) remove with a callback per removed node; stackless preorder, postorder, children, ancestors and a skipping walk; sylva::Error for failures; to_tree exports to sylva::tree::Tree. (2) Flat: a preorder index (every slot in preorder, where each subtree ends) plus contiguous child lists, rebuilt O(n) without allocating only when Forest::version changed; full passes read the preorder array, skipping walks read the child lists with a reusable stack. (3) Column<T>: per-node data by slot, structure-of-arrays. Measured on 10k/100k-node trees (16 children per node) against a hand-written arena with a child Vec per node: full preorder 0.66/6.5 us vs 9.1/103 us (about 14x faster); dirty walk with 1% dirty 1.6/16.3 us vs 1.64/17.1 us (equal or faster); build 135-146 us/1.13 ms vs 65-78 us/1.02-1.07 ms (about 10% slower at 100k, the one gap: worth a look); Flat rebuild 42/422 us; sylva's Tree builds about 10x slower than either. Also needed for parda to publish: uuid optional (or not on this module's path), no_std + alloc friendly if cheap, wasm-compatible, published to crates.io under the library combination.

Answer (planned): Planned as sylva / Structures / Forest, beside Tree; your crates/sylva-forest (parda2D 7912896) is the starting point when it moves in. Its rules carry what you list: generational ids that fail safely, O(1) links with nothing allocated per node, columns by slot, allocation-free walks, no uuid or serde on its path with no_std + alloc and wasm32, and benchmarks against a hand-written arena (the 10% build gap at 100k is noted). Flat and Column come in with it. The crate-wide parts are todos here: uuid behind a default feature, no_std + alloc with a wasm32 check, and publishing to crates.io under the library combo, which is the user's step. Follow the node for when it lands.
